newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura's JGB underwriting share to be distributed.
newsitem.headline: Nomura's JGB underwriting share to be distributed.

text.p: Nomura Securities Co Ltd's share of underwriting 10-year Japanese government bonds (JGBs) will be divided up among other brokerages in the JGB underwriting group, an underwriting source at Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd, lead-manager of the group, said on Thursday.
The Ministry of Finance suspended Nomura Securities from underwriting JGBs after Japan's securities watchdog filed a criminal complaint with prosecutors against the brokerage on Tuesday evening.
The source said that the share each brokerage will get will depend on the firm's current underwriting ratio within the group.

Sources said the group of securities houses currently has a 32.21 percent share of the 10-year JGB underwriting business. The rest of the business is split among banks, insurers and other financial institutions.
Of the group's total share, Nomura had 18.55 percent of the business, the sources said.

When the MOF offers 10-year JGBs every month, 60 percent of the offered volume is sold through a price-competitive auction. The rest is sold to underwriters depending on each firm's underwriting ratio. The ratio is revised regularly.
All of the five-year discount government bonds are sold in the latter manner.
Sources said the group of securities houses currently take a share of 61.1 percent of the five-year discount bond underwriting business.
Of the group's total share, Nomura had 20.00 percent of the business, the sources said.
The MOF currently offers the other types of JGBs through price-competitive auctions.
